summary: An explicit restart closes a failed runtime start that never proved its producer closed once it is older than any launcher could still publish, so a seat parked after a failed launch can be restarted, and a member pass that started nothing no longer records 'member-recovered'

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes for completed operations. A restart request that waits on a pending start now records a 'restart-waiting' reconcile decision, and a failed unverified start older than 15 minutes is closed under the kernel start lock when no runtime of the seat is running.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. The existing producer-closure transition is reused.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Two new reconcile decision names ('restart-waiting', 'restart-superseded-failed-start') and one ('member-pass-clean') appear in runtime.reconcile-decision claims; readers that treat any decision other than 'member-fault' as a cleared fault are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No additional startup work or expected interruption.

manual.detail: No operator actions are required; an already parked seat is released by its next explicit restart on a daemon with this change.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new swap-back restrictions.
